15 Cool Places to Visit in Saskatchewan

TL;DR

Saskatchewan is more than flat land and endless fields. It’s a province filled with lakes, parks, cultural landmarks, and hidden gems that make it a dream for travelers. For travel nurses, these spots are a perfect way to balance demanding shifts with adventure and downtime. This guide takes you through 15 must-see places in Saskatchewan and shows how exploring them can fit beautifully into your travel nursing journey.

Key Highlights

  • Discover lakes, parks, and cities that bring Saskatchewan to life.
  • Learn how travel nurses can mix work with exploration.
  • Get practical tips for making the most of every assignment in the province.
  • Understand why Goodwill Staffing makes travel nursing in Saskatchewan simple and rewarding.

When most people think about Saskatchewan, they picture endless wheat fields stretching under a wide blue sky. That’s not wrong, but it’s only part of the story.

The real Saskatchewan is packed with lakes, forests, national parks, and vibrant cities just waiting to be explored.

Here’s the problem: travelers skip over this province because they think there’s nothing exciting here. That’s a mistake. The solution? Dive into this list of 15 cool places that prove Saskatchewan is bursting with adventure.

If you’re a travel nurse, this isn’t just a list of fun spots; it’s a guide to what your downtime could look like while you’re working assignments across the province.

1. Prince Albert National Park

Prince Albert National Park is Saskatchewan’s pride. It mixes wild forest with sandy beaches and clear lakes. You can hike through boreal woodland, kayak on Waskesiu Lake, or even spot bison roaming freely.

  • Perfect for: long weekend breaks.
  • Travel nurse perk: outdoor escapes after demanding shifts. Nature restores your energy faster than any nap.

2. Wascana Centre, Regina

Wascana Centre is one of the largest urban parks in North America. It stretches across Regina with gardens, trails, and lakeside paths. You’ll find the Saskatchewan Legislative Building here, making it both scenic and historic.

  • Perfect for: evening walks after work.
  • Travel nurse perk: quick access to relaxation in the middle of a city assignment.

3. Grasslands National Park

Grasslands National Park feels untouched. Wide open skies, rolling prairie, and wildlife like bison and prairie dogs make it unique. At night, the skies explode with stars, making it a Dark Sky Preserve.

  • Perfect for: stargazing weekends.
  • Travel nurse perk: a reminder that quiet places heal burnout.

4. Wanuskewin Heritage Park

Wanuskewin near Saskatoon tells the story of Indigenous peoples who lived on these lands for thousands of years. With art, cultural programs, and archaeological sites, it’s more than a tourist stop—it’s history you can feel.

  • Perfect for: cultural days off.
  • Travel nurse perk: a deeper understanding of the communities you serve.

5. Little Manitou Lake

This lake has so much mineral salt that you float without effort. It’s like Canada’s Dead Sea. Locals believe the waters have healing powers, and even if you’re skeptical, it’s a relaxing experience.

  • Perfect for: soothing sore muscles after shifts.
  • Travel nurse perk: natural stress relief between contracts.

6. Cypress Hills Interprovincial Park

Cypress Hills is different from the flat prairie around it. Hills, forests, lakes, and meadows stretch as far as you can see. It’s a hotspot for camping, hiking, and wildlife watching.

  • Perfect for: adventurous long weekends.
  • Travel nurse perk: recharging in a place that feels nothing like work.

7. Moose Jaw Tunnels

Under the streets of Moose Jaw, a network of tunnels tells stories of history. History of Chinese immigrants, Al Capone’s rumored bootlegging, and more. Guided tours make it an adventure underground.

  • Perfect for: fun days off.
  • Travel nurse perk: unique experiences that turn small assignments into big memories.

8. Saskatoon River Landing

Saskatoon’s River Landing is modern and buzzing. Cafés, trails, and cultural spaces line the river, making it a favorite hangout. Evening strolls or weekend markets make this a city highlight.

  • Perfect for: city breaks during assignments.
  • Travel nurse perk: vibrant city life mixed with relaxation.

9. Athabasca Sand Dunes

You don’t expect massive sand dunes in Saskatchewan, but the Athabasca Sand Dunes are one of the largest active dune fields in North America. They’re remote, wild, and breathtaking.

  • Perfect for: adventurous explorers.
  • Travel nurse perk: ultimate reward after tough rotations.

10. Batoche National Historic Site

Batoche preserves Métis history and tells the story of the 1885 North-West Resistance. Walking through the site feels like stepping back in time.

  • Perfect for: history lovers.
  • Travel nurse perk: connection to Canada’s deeper cultural roots.

11. Fort Walsh National Historic Site

This historic fort in Cypress Hills shares stories of the North West Mounted Police. It’s both educational and scenic, surrounded by rolling hills.

  • Perfect for: learning and exploring in one trip.
  • Travel nurse perk: meaningful downtime that feels bigger than tourism.

12. Qu’Appelle Valley

The Qu’Appelle Valley surprises visitors with its lakes and hills carved by glaciers. It’s a hotspot for boating, hiking, and lakefront relaxation.

  • Perfect for: water lovers.
  • Travel nurse perk: quick weekend escape near Regina.

13. Royal Saskatchewan Museum

This museum in Regina showcases natural history, from dinosaur skeletons to Indigenous history exhibits. It’s interactive, so it’s great for learning without feeling like a lecture.

  • Perfect for: rainy day adventures.
  • Travel nurse perk: stress-free fun when you don’t feel like hiking.

14. Meadow Lake Provincial Park

Meadow Lake has over 20 lakes, countless trails, and endless camping opportunities. It’s the ultimate outdoor retreat in northern Saskatchewan.

  • Perfect for: nature-packed holidays.
  • Travel nurse perk: a full reset after months of shifts.

15. Saskatoon Forestry Farm Park & Zoo

This is both a park and a small zoo. It’s quiet, family-friendly, and a great way to unwind without leaving the city.

  • Perfect for: laid-back afternoons.
  • Travel nurse perk: easy stress relief during city assignments.

Why These Spots Matter for Travel Nurses

Being a travel nurse is demanding. Long shifts, new environments, and constant adjustment can wear you down. That’s why Saskatchewan’s hidden gems matter. They give you balance.

  • After a 12-hour shift, walking along Wascana Lake clears your head.
  • A weekend in Grasslands helps you breathe under the stars.
  • A day trip to Wanuskewin deepens your cultural awareness.

Work may bring you here, but adventure keeps you grounded.

FAQs

Is Saskatchewan worth visiting for travel nurses?
Yes. Between assignments and shifts, you’ll find endless outdoor escapes, cultural landmarks, and small-town gems.

Can I travel on my days off while working in Saskatchewan?
Definitely. Most facilities schedule shifts to allow proper downtime, and weekend trips are common.

Which city should I choose for assignments?
Saskatoon and Regina are top picks, but smaller towns near parks and lakes also offer rewarding experiences.

To Wrap It Up

Saskatchewan is full of life. National parks and sand dunes to cultural sites and buzzing cities, there’s always something to see. For travel nurses, these aren’t just attractions; they’re ways to recharge, find balance, and make every assignment memorable.
